I used my PS4 controller wired for PC play, but I've read that you can buy third party bluetooth adapters to get it to work wirelessly. Xbox one controller is hands down the best gamepad you can get for your money right now. Works wired, requires no drivers or setup to work with Windows. Can be used wirelessly with a dongle later if you change your mind.

I have a steam controller also, and it's a compelling choice due to its flexibility - but only if you're willing to put the effort in to learning a new controller layout and you're OK with a lot of initial configuration for games. This controller is almost always very awkward for people at first.

One point in favor of the XB1 controller is that the XB1 headset plugs in to the controller and can be used with Windows as a speaker and microphone input which can be convenient. Not a huge deal though - most people have their own preferred headset so whether or not this appeals to you is a bit of a personal thing.

The biggest differences between the XB1 and the PS4 controllers are button and stick layout. Both are of excellent build quality. Both can be made to work with Windows. I personally think the XB1 controller is better. Opinions will vary, I would suggest at least holding both in your hands before you make a choice.

Can you elaborate what's so flexible about the Steam controller? I mean, I'm guessing I can change some buttons preferences on the other controllers as well.

It's difficult to explain it all, because the configuration is .. overwhelmingly deep. Suffice to say there at a fuckton of ways to configure it's behaviors. The trackpads can be made to emulate mice, or joysticks, or can do crazy shit like simulate a mouse for something that only supports a joystick input. It has a crazy-accurate gyroscope in it that many find very useful for FPS aiming. It's got more buttons than the typical gamepad - sporting two more buttons on the rear of the case. It can be configured for macro operations. It can support shift operations where pressing a button changes the mappings for other buttons. It has a bunch of settings for changing all of the acceleration ramps for movement. Configurations get cloud saved with your steam account. If you plug in your steam controller at your friends place and log in to steam, it will load all your configurations. The list of things it can do is long, and I'd never cover it all.

There are probably some videos that showcase more of the configuration, but believe me when I say it's exhaustive. They tried to think of everything, and they might be close to having a kitchen sink installed some day.

Before getting a controller, you should consider what games you want to use it for and which one you think is the most comfortable. Maybe go to a retail store and see what feels best. Kind of like trying on clothes, it's personal preference and a bit hard to judge over the internet.

I just purchased a steam controller recently. With about 2 weeks experience, I would highly recommend it. Arcade games should work very well on it and it is the most customized and innovative controller currently on the market so changing it to your needs should be a breeze. There are also user imported control schemes for TONS of games so you can always work with a template and go from there.

Also, if you ever plan on branching out and playing more "PC" centric games, the steam controller hands down is the only controller with the capabilities to actually play and enjoy pc games that usually require mouse/keyboard input. What I mean by that, is that the ps4/xbone controllers don't have the technology or breadth of variability that the steam controller has. It isn't the best controller for every game, but it's the best controller for ALL games, regardless of platform or controller input.

Good luck in your decision.
